newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says Israel, U.S. main foes, others secondary.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Israel, U.S. main foes, others secondary.

text.p: Iran's supreme leader moved on Wednesday to defuse a row with Germany over terrorism charges against Tehran, saying Israel and the United States were Iran's main foes and the hostility of others was secondary.
"Our main enemy is made up of these two filthy and evil elements: the Great Satan (U.S.) and the Zionists," Ayatollah Ali Khamenei said in a speech broadcast on Tehran radio.
"The Iranian nation will not be misled...: any other persons or governments which engage in hostility are secondary and incidental," he said.

Khamenei did not name Germany but analysts said he appeared to be trying to defuse tension between Iran and its main trade partner over a German prosecutor's accusation that Khamenei and other Tehran officials ordered the killing of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator at a Berlin restaurant in 1992.
Khamenei stressed that Israel and the United States were the main backers of Baghdad in the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
Some Iranian officials and groups have accused Germany of delivering missiles and chemical weapons to Iraq during the war. Germany rejected the allegations.

State-run Tehran radio said slogans against Israel and the United States were the main chants in a demonstration against the German charges held on Wednesday by Islamic seminary students and teachers in the holy city of Qom.

Newspapers reported several demonstrations across Iran to protest against the charges. They carried statements by various groups, with some radical groups urging the government to sever ties with Germany if it does not apologise for the accusations.

The row threatens trade ties worth $1.4 billion last year between Iran and Germany. Also at risk is the European Union's "critical dialogue" with Iran which Bonn has promoted as an alternative to U.S. sanctions aimed at isolating Tehran.

Tehran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings and officially protested on Thursday to Bonn over the charges. German prosecutors have demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese who were tried for the killings.
